title: How should a workout page work? (Munich '72)
question: Three page structures for the workout pages, shown as phone wireframes. Lock one, steer, or re-roll.

options.label: Swipe Deck
options.thesis: Pick Pull 1 or Pull 2, then swipe sideways through the session: one big exercise card per screen, the next one peeking in.
options.viewport: Light-blue band 'Pull' with pictogram; tabs Pull 1 | Pull 2; a card filling the screen: animation on top, name + big dose, muscle + Feel, numbered cues; next card's edge peeking right; dots below.
options.risk: Background/rationale prose must live elsewhere (a 'Why' drawer), or the cards get long.

options.label: Step-Through
options.thesis: A guided session: a strip of exercise ticks across the top, one exercise below, big Prev / Next buttons at thumb height.
materials: progress strip of ticks (done marks persist)
options.viewport: Band with section + session picker; tick strip 1·2·3·4 (done ones filled green); the current exercise: animation, name + dose, muscle + Feel, numbered cues; Prev / Done & Next at the bottom.
options.risk: Feels app-like; scanning the whole session at once takes one tap on the strip.

options.label: Programme List
options.thesis: The whole session as an event programme: rows with a small looping animation, name and dose; tap a row to open it in place.
options.viewport: Band + tabs; a list of 4–5 rows (thumb · name · dose · done tick); the open row grows to show the full animation, muscle + Feel and numbered cues; others stay compact.
options.risk: Least 'one thing at a time'; mid-set you have to find and open the right row.
